vascular_cognitive_impairment.summary: No disease-modifying therapy exists for vascular cognitive impairment; management is control of the vascular risk factors, secondary prevention matched to the mechanism, review of the anticholinergic burden, and treatment of coexisting Alzheimer pathology where biomarkers support it.

prohibited_recommendations: Do not scan a patient with a non-MR-conditional pacemaker and unavailable device documentation, particularly when pacing-dependent with complete atrioventricular block
Do not fit an external rhythm monitor when the implanted device already stores twelve months of atrial data
Do not present a CT-based diagnosis as equivalent to an MRI-based one — record the limitations, especially the inability to exclude amyloid angiopathy
Do not continue aspirin alongside a new anticoagulant without a separate indication
Do not withhold anticoagulation solely because microbleed status is unknown, but do document the uncertainty and the discussion
required_recommendations: Confirm the MR-conditional status of the device and document why MRI cannot be performed rather than simply omitting it
Obtain CT and state explicitly what it cannot show — microbleeds, cortical superficial siderosis and medial temporal atrophy grade
Interrogate the pacemaker: it holds twelve months of continuous atrial rhythm data and outperforms any external monitor
Image the carotid arteries, since duplex ultrasound is unaffected by the device
Make the anticoagulation decision explicitly, acknowledging that the haemorrhagic risk cannot be fully assessed without gradient-echo imaging
Refer for revascularisation assessment of a symptomatic 60-70% stenosis and treat both mechanisms

avoided_actions.rationale: EEG has no diagnostic role in vascular cognitive impairment; it belongs to the differential of a rapidly progressive or fluctuating course (Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease, non-convulsive status, toxic-metabolic encephalopathy), none of which is present here

A presynaptic dopaminergic study answers the Lewy-body question, not the vascular one, and there is no spontaneous parkinsonism, no fluctuating cognition with hallucinations and no REM sleep behaviour disorder
Cardiac sympathetic imaging is a test for dementia with Lewy bodies and for autonomic failure; it says nothing about cerebrovascular disease

An untargeted paraneoplastic or autoimmune-encephalitis battery in a chronic stepwise decline with a hypertensive imaging burden is the archetypal expensive miss; the indication for those assays is a subacute multidomain syndrome

The pacemaker and leads are not MR-conditional and the manufacturer's documentation is unavailable, so scanning risks lead heating, device damage and arrhythmia in a pacing-dependent patient with complete atrioventricular block; severe claustrophobia is an additional obstacle

accepted: Vascular dementia — multi-infarct type from symptomatic left internal carotid stenosis with coexisting paroxysmal atrial fibrillation documented on pacemaker interrogation; diagnosed on CT because MRI is contraindicated

differential.key_features: Cannot be excluded, because CT cannot grade medial temporal atrophy and the patient cannot have an MRI; recall is cue-responsive and the profile is executive and language-led, which argues against it, and the diagnostic limitation should be stated rather than hidden

Cannot be excluded on CT, which cannot show microbleeds or cortical superficial siderosis; this is the limitation that matters most, because it bears directly on the safety of the anticoagulation the atrial fibrillation indicates
Periventricular low attenuation is present but cannot be graded reliably on CT, and the two cortical infarcts with a stepwise history are the substrate
Paroxysmal atrial fibrillation is documented, but both cortical infarcts are ipsilateral to a 60-70% stenosis, so a large-artery mechanism is at least as likely and both need treating

differential.diagnosis: Recurrent transient ischaemic attacks without infarction
differential.key_features: Two chronic cortical infarcts are visible on CT

key_clinical_evidence: A contraindication to the best test is a clinical problem to be worked around and documented, not a reason to leave the diagnosis unstated: CT plus the clinical course plus duplex plus device data reached a mechanism-level diagnosis here
The device in the patient is the best rhythm monitor available to him — twelve months of continuous stored atrial data at no additional cost and with no additional procedure

What CT cannot see is the clinically important part: microbleeds and siderosis bear directly on the safety of the anticoagulation the atrial fibrillation indicates, and that uncertainty must be named in the record and in the consent discussion
Two ipsilateral cortical infarcts downstream of a 60-70% stenosis and a documented 2.1% atrial fibrillation burden are two mechanisms, and each carries its own treatment
Stating a diagnostic limitation is part of the diagnosis; presenting a CT-based attribution as complete would misrepresent what is known

ct.impression: Two chronic left middle cerebral artery territory cortical infarcts, one right subcortical lacune and moderate periventricular low attenuation. Sufficient to attribute the dementia to cerebrovascular disease. Explicit limitations: microbleeds and cortical superficial siderosis are invisible on CT, so amyloid angiopathy is not excluded, and medial temporal atrophy cannot be graded, so a coexisting degenerative process is neither supported nor excluded.

patient.history_present_illness: Mr. Ottavio Pirelli is a 79-year-old retired customs officer who attends with his wife. She dates his decline to two events: two years ago he had an hour of right arm weakness, and eight months ago a day of right hand clumsiness with word-finding difficulty. Neither was imaged. After each he was permanently worse, and between them he was stable. He now cannot manage the household accounts he kept for decades, has twice missed medication doses, and stopped driving eight months ago. His memory improves when he is reminded of context; his difficulty is with organising and with finding words. He has a dual-chamber pacemaker implanted eleven years ago for complete atrioventricular block; the device is not MR-conditional and the manufacturer's documentation cannot be located, and he also has severe claustrophobia. There are no hallucinations, no fluctuation in alertness and no dream enactment. His blood pressure runs at 150-160 systolic.

neurological_exam.additional: Pacemaker box palpable below the left clavicle. Pulse regular at 68, paced. No carotid bruit. No frontal release signs.

neurological_exam.motor: Increased tone in the right arm. Strength 5-/5 right hand, otherwise 5/5. Right pronator drift.
neurological_exam.sensory: Reduced graphaesthesia in the right hand.
